status.en: 141 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Abuja, Lagos and Kaduna.
status.nb: 141 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Abuja, Lagos og Kaduna.

summary.en: Bandits continue to target civilians and mining operations in Plateau, killing three at a mining site and later killing nine in a separate attack, while also kidnapping six people and stealing livestock in Sokoto. Nigerian security forces are confronting bandits in Kwara and have seized uniforms and military caps from them in northern forests, and they rescued 125 kidnapping victims and dismantled terrorist camps, killing 21 ISWAP fighters in Borno. Police are searching for the family of a Canadian-Nigerian man killed in a road crash near Lagos Airport. The conflict recorded 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Bandittene fortsetter å angripe sivile og gruvevirksomheter i Plateau, dreper tre på en gruveplass og senere ni i et separat angrep, samtidig som de kidnapper seks personer og stjeler husdyr i Sokoto. Nigerias sikkerhetsstyrker konfronterer banditter i Kwara og har beslaglagt uniformer og militære luer fra dem i nordlige skoger, og de reddet 125 kidnappingsofre og demonterte terrorleirer, og drepte 21 ISWAP-krigere i Borno. Politiet leter etter familien til en kanadisk-nigeriansk mann som ble drept i en veitrafikkulykke nær Lagos flyplass. Konflikten registrerte 1 486 dødsfall knyttet til kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
